claim: The episode examines the claim that lab supplied harnesses benefit from model post training on their tool formats.
The speakers argue that even a small per call advantage can compound across 50 to 500 tool calls.
A model provider can post train for a chosen tool shape, so the surface syntax itself need not be intrinsically optimal.
Recursive types and discriminated unions still impose structured generation constraints unless the model has special training for them.
A harness binary that runs user code on the user's machine exposes behavior that can be inspected.
The speakers place most builder advantage in outer orchestration and domain context rather than cloning a lab's inner coding loop.
note: This is a synthesis across the later discussion.
